from.place: proof step 2: restriction of the big fppf sheafification to affine objects

title: The affine fppf site is a dense subsite of the big fppf site
statement: Let $S$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme]. Let $\mathcal C=(\mathit{Aff}/S)_{fppf}$ be the site of affine $S$-schemes with fppf coverings and let $\mathcal D=(\mathit{Sch}/S)_{fppf}$ be the big fppf site [def-pc-fppf-site]. The inclusion $u:\mathcal C\to\mathcal D$ is dense: every object of $\mathcal D$ has an fppf covering by objects of $\mathcal C$, and every fppf covering of an affine object admits a refinement by a covering in $\mathcal C$. Consequently restriction along $u$ induces an equivalence between sheaves of sets on $\mathcal D$ and sheaves of sets on $\mathcal C$ (and likewise for abelian sheaves), with quasi-inverse given by sheaf transport along the dense inclusion.

proof.text: The inclusion u is fully faithful because (Aff/S) is the full subcategory of (Sch/S) on affine objects, so morphisms in C are exactly the S-morphisms between the same schemes in D.

Every object $X \to S$ of the big site has a covering family by affine objects: choose an affine open covering of X, and regard each open immersion $U_i \to X$ as an S-morphism. Open immersions are flat and locally of finite presentation, hence fppf, and the images cover X by lem-pc-fppf-affine-open-cover.

For an affine object U and any fppf covering family $\{T_i \to U\}$, lem-pc-fppf-affine-refinement supplies finitely many affine opens V_j contained in members T_{i(j)} whose composites $V_j \to U$ are fppf and jointly surjective. These morphisms form a covering in the affine fppf site and refine the original covering.

The preceding two clauses say that u is cover-dense and that the topology on C is the topology induced from D: a sieve on an affine U covers in C exactly when the sieve generated by its image under u covers u(U) in D. Applying the dense-subsite theorem lem-pc-fppf-dense-sheaf-equivalence gives an equivalence of sheaves of sets, and applying it with abelian groups gives the same equivalence for abelian sheaves.
